title: Greater Norwich NSSA -New Settlement Master Planning - Town Planning and Landscape - AWARD
description:
Greater Norwich, comprising the local authorities of South Norfolk Council (SNC), Broadland District Council (BDC) and Norwich City Council (NCC), also working with Norfolk County Council (Norfolk CC), has an established track record of partnership working in the context of plan-making, strategic infrastructure planning and investment.   
      The potential for delivery of a new settlement, or settlements, in the Greater Norwich area was considered during the preparation of the, now adopted, Greater Norwich Local Plan (GNLP).   Whilst none of the potential new settlement sites considered were allocated, the adopted GNLP identified that any review of the local plan in the future would assess the potential for a new settlement or settlements.   
      In the context of a proposed GNLP Review, the Greater Norwich Development Partnership (GNDP) has recently committed to developing an evidence base and exploring the potential allocation of land for a new settlement or settlements. It is also likely, ahead of a likely devolution process, that Norfolk and Suffolk will be embarking on the creation of a strategic Spatial Development Strategy (SDS) so there is a further imperative to consider strategic growth opportunities for Greater Norwich, positioned within a wider context. 
      This consultancy appointment is being jointly commissioned by SNC and BDC, on behalf of the GNDP. 
      A Call for Sites has been undertaken (Spring '26) in preparation for the GNLP Review - with the new plan being prepared in accordance with the new plan-making system - and three potential new settlement sites have been promoted. These are the same sites promoted through the last plan-making process. 
      The purpose of this commission is to procure a consultant to provide strategic Master planning and Landscape advice to support in 'triaging' three potential new settlement sites to inform the Site Assessment process and the identification of preferred new settlement site(s) prior to the proposed Regulation 23 Consultation.

description:

The scope of the contract includes installation of ramped access path from Ladbrook Place and resurfacing and refit of the step path from Kett's Hill entrance. The materials required for the project will need to be transferred from the car park to the construction area in a safe and effective way (crane/other equipment/other method). Also, as there is a gas main pipe on site the winning contractor will also have to work alongside Cadent Gas who will be overseeing the project.

The University of East Anglia (UEA) is an internationally renowned university based in a campus that provides top quality academic, social and cultural facilities to students and staff.       Located in 320 acres of rolling parkland but just two miles from the centre of the cathedral city of Norwich the University is adjacent to the Norwich Research Park which is home to over 1,000 scientists working in several world ranked institutions.
      
      As of 2021, a total of 17,161 students are currently studying at the University: 13,396 undergraduates and 3,765 postgraduates. Of these, over 3,500 are non-UK students from more than 100 countries worldwide. The University employs approximately 3,700 staff, a third of whom work part-time. More than 1,500 staff are academic (including approx. 370 researchers) and the rest are administrative, technical or general staff.
      
      Founded in 1963 and located on a single campus (the "Campus") on the western fringe of Norwich, the University is ranked as one of the United Kingdom's foremost higher education and research institutions enjoying an international reputation for excellence in many of its disciplines.  As a consequence of its reputation, the University continues to grow.
      
      The University's academic record is matched by its fine campus.  Laid out to a Master Plan by Sir Denys Lasdun, many of the early buildings were designed by him.  These have been added to by subsequent generations of architects, all of whom have left their distinctive mark.  They include for example, Feilden and Mawson, Arup Associates, Foster and Partners, Mather Associates, John Miller and Partners, R H Partnership, RMJM, Shepheard Epstein Hunter, LSI Architects and more recently Architype, Pick Everard and Hawkins Brown.  In its short history, the University can boast in excess of 30 Architectural and civic Trust Awards.  As a consequence, English Heritage takes a keen interest in the University's refurbishment programme and new buildings.  In October 2003 the core buildings of the Campus were Grade II and Grade II* Listed and, in 2006 the ground breaking Conservation Development Strategy received formal support from the Norwich City Planning Committee.  In 2012 the iconic Sainsbury Centre for Visual Arts was also Grade II* Listed.
      
      As a single campus university with a student population in the region of 17,000, the Campus operates as an autonomous community. The inherent flexibility of the original buildings and the quality of the Campus generally has provided a sound basis for adaptation.
